experiment_data.hypothesis: Conformal-guided auxiliary loss (lambda=0.1) will improve CRM by encouraging correction magnitude proportional to nonconformity, compared to uniform MSE
experiment_data.notes: Training completed cleanly (50/50 epochs, EXIT_CODE=0). Val loss decreased monotonically 0.037526 (ep1) → 0.013343 (ep50). Final train_loss=0.016046, val_loss=0.013343. The ~6.4x higher val_loss vs MSE baseline (0.013343 vs 0.002080) is EXPECTED and NOT a regression: total loss = MSE + λ·conformal_aux with λ=0.1, so the reported loss is on a strictly larger objective than the MSE-only baseline — direct numeric comparison is invalid. Convergence shape is healthy (still improving at ep50, no divergence). Whether the conformal-guided regularizer actually helps the CRM produce more useful corrections must be judged on downstream robot eval (success rate on SmolVLA Object), not on training-objective loss. Best ckpt saved.
